name: Josiah Taylor
strengths: Taylor already carries a true heavy-interior frame at 6-4 / 313 — length and mass to occupy doubles as a young DL.
Taylor shows active hands when engaging blockers in line work, using the frame to create early contact instead of catching.
Taylor plays with a steady motor through the whistle on interior reps — effort matches the size on early snaps.
weaknesses: Taylor still needs lower pad level and cleaner footwork so taller mass does not get stood up into blockers.
Taylor’s counter package vs double teams is raw — must add violence and reset moves before every-down SEC claims stick.
comparison: Taylor comps to Kenny Clark — listed 6-4 / 313 vs Clark’s ~6-3 / 314 interior mold (height within ~1", same heavy DT frame); then matching occupy-and-disrupt tools from early tape (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Taylor projects to develop into Florida’s DL room with Year-1 practice / early-down depth snaps, Year-2 compete for a rotational 3-tech / nose role, and Year-3+ starter upside as a two-gap interior if pad level and hand counters catch the mass.
schemeFit: Taylor fits an even front that wants a heavy shade / 3-tech who can eat doubles, two-gap early downs, and still push the pocket as the hands catch up.

recruitingStory: Josiah Taylor is an in-state DL listed 6-4 / 313 from Vero Beach (FL) — Florida-offer heavy interior with live UF chase heat after FNL.
angle: True 300+ in-state interior body — Florida can develop the hands into a starter-upside DT.
insiderNotes: Watched Vero Beach QwikCut tape (#75). Taylor’s win right now is the frame + effort; polish pad level and double-team counters.
